title: Making a sci-fi deckbuilder for Android using Codex, Claude Code and Astra
author: RiftcoilDev
selftext:
Hey everyone!

We're a team of two working on Riftcoil, a sci-fi roguelike deckbuilder for Android.



# About the game:

The game combines card-based combat with reactor management. Each turn, you distribute power between weapons, shields, engines and utility systems.

The game has branching expeditions, multiple ships, commanders and deckbuilding progression.

The full campaign (3 sectors) is free to play, works offline, and has no ads or subscriptions. There's an optional one-time expansion pack.



# Dev process ( with no previous game dev experience and basic Kotlin knowledge)

1. Creating prototype document using ChatGPT project (Sol/High)

2. New project in Android Studio 

3. Using Codex/Claude code CLI in IDE, all pixel art work was generated by Astra, coding on Sol/High or Opus 5/5.5 - medium 

4. Testing on Pixel 7 emulator and real device using Wireless debugging 



# Things that took most time:

1. UI - both ChatGPT/Claude were horrible with it and required multiple checks, even now it looks a bit rough

2. Balancing - AI can't play your game well,  so you need to do play tests on your own each time there is a significant change (new commander, enemies, ships , sectors etc) . That took even more time than coding tbh. 

3. New mechanics - while AI can help with brainstorming, you still have to come up with something that would be actually fun for the player, and feel new. 

For example, AI suggested to charge player for removing the cards like in popular deckbuilders, but in sci-fi/space setting it doesn't make any sense - there are no "cursed cards", so instead you can scrap the cards you don't need for salvage (basic game currency) 

4. Checking artwork and descriptions - drones with propellers flying in space, ships facing different direction, confusing card descriptions etc. 

Game is available on **Google Play:** [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.akkeros.riftcoil](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.akkeros.riftcoil) , 

Also if you have Google account, you can play it on PC using [Google Play Games](https://google.play/games/en-us/) 

Small interactive demo is available on website [https://playriftcoil.com/](https://playriftcoil.com/) 

Would be interested to hear any feedback, particularly from any deckbuilder games fans
